For F0 bounded below and fixed sufficiently large alpha, division by F0 and integration by parts give coercivity, since alpha^2 dominates the bounded remaining potential. Equations (5.7),(5.13),(5.14) make f=derivative(-H1[A]/F) zero near Yc: chi1=0,chi=1 and the remaining integral is constant there. Away from Yc the forcing and coefficients converge to real values. Choosing ci(alpha) sufficiently small along a diagonal contradicts the proposed positive lower bound while retaining all upper smallness constraints.
